correctness.rationale: Bézout and the restriction of quadrics to a smooth conic give an exhaustive normal form; coordinate automorphisms determine a complete invariant. Explicit pairwise intersection equations give the entire singularity basket. An identity for a cubic Jacobian syzygy and a nonzero 18-by-18 determinant for every kappa != 0,1 prove mdr=3; a special quadratic syzygy and nonzero 17-by-17 minor at kappa=1 prove mdr=2. The numerical free/near-free criteria apply at d=6; all symbolic identities were executed with the embedded checker. Limits: complex, smooth, nondegenerate conics only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2025 work restricts to free arrangements, and Pokora theorem 3.2 imposes a deformation and mdr condition. Neither broader-looking result classifies the nonfree members and their stabilizers nor automatically verifies mdr=3 for all nonzero nonunit parameters.

originality.rationale: The prior papers establish the extremal two-A7 bound, one free configuration and one nearly-free deformation, and classify free three-conic arrangements. A two-conic A7 equation is known. The new claim is the full unordered three-conic projective moduli with unique product invariant, uniform near-free locus, and full stabilizer. No inspected source supplies or implies these together; indexed searches returned distinct objects or more restricted cases. Historical and unindexed formula risk remains.
residual_risks: Persson 1982 original full text not materially inspected; formulas there might admit an equivalent global parametrization.
Megyesi 2000 and older conic-configuration classifications could contain an equivalent moduli invariant in another notation; not confirmed.
Unindexed mathematical literature and unpublished work cannot be excluded by indexed queries.

value.rationale: The class realizes the maximal A7 count for three smooth conics, a natural extremal geometric locus highlighted by the literature. The result gives its exact coarse projective parameter and stabilizer uniformly and classifies every smooth member as free or nearly free by a sharp single-point transition. This is a complete motivated geometric and homological classification, not one isolated calculation or restatement of known examples.
